newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Alongside sister markets in Europe, Spanish government bonds ended sharply higher on Tuesday as a German government-Bundesbank deal on gold revaluation helped spark a short squeeze.
"Once more the market is pricing in the best of all worlds -- a timely and softer EMU, despite higher interest rates," a Madrid-based dealer said.
Others agreed, saying the Spanish market would show a "new record high short-run, after the U.S. job data on Friday".
Sweden's choice to stay out of the launch of Europe's single currency was not affecting Spain's debt market, dealers added.
Earlier on Tuesday, Germany's parliament retreated from a controversial plan to revalue the central bank's gold reserves.
"The market reacted well to the news but I do not expect this is going to last in the medium term," a dealer said.
Whether Germany went ahead with a softer EMU or introduced fiscal measures such as a tax hike, this would probably create political tensions, he added.
The Spanish 10-year spread versus Bunds fell to around 72 basis points at the close after having traded at 75 basis points earlier.
The spread hit a record low at 64 basis points on May 21.
"I do not expect the spread to fall more than that, until we are sure that the Bank of Spain will cut its key rate further," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, trader at ABN Amro.
Other dealers said they expected the Bank of Spain to cut its official rate by 25 basis points to 5.00 percent as soon as second half June, after the June 13 release of May CPI.
Earlier, the Spanish Treasury allotted three- and 10-year bonds at lower yields than one month ago.
"The Treasury's auctions were a success and the second part tomorrow will also go smoothly," a dealer in Madrid said.
The Treasury is selling five-, 15-year bonds and six-month bills on Wednesday.
